question: Which island group lies to the south-east of the Indian mainland? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Agatti island
Minicoy
Andaman and Nicobar
Lakshadweep
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Andaman and Nicobar

Explanation:
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands group lies to the south-east of the Indian mainland in the Bay of Bengal. It is a union territory of India consisting of about 572 islands. The nearest point on the Indian mainland is Cape Comorin. This group is divided into two parts: the Andaman Islands in the north and the Nicobar Islands in the south. Its capital is Port Blair. The region is known for its rich biodiversity and marine life. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The highest peak in the region is Saddle Peak (732 meters).

☛ Water body separating Andaman and Nicobar → Ten Degree Channel
☛ Highest point in Andaman → Saddle Peak
☛ Southernmost point of Indian mainland → Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari)
☛ Approximate number of islands in Andaman and Nicobar → 572
question_hi: भारतीय मुख्य भूमि के दक्षिण-पूर्व में कौन सा द्वीप समूह स्थित है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following crops is grown in waterlogged conditions? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Maize
Bajra
Groundnut
Rice
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rice

Explanation:
Rice (paddy) is a crop that is grown under waterlogged conditions. It is known as a wetland crop because its cultivation requires fields to be submerged in 10-15 cm of water. The roots of rice contain aerenchyma tissue that facilitates oxygen transport, enabling the plant to survive in flooded conditions. Rice is a staple food for a large portion of the world's population, especially in Asia. It requires high temperatures and heavy rainfall for growth. Other crops like maize, bajra, and groundnut cannot tolerate waterlogging and need well-drained soils. Rice is typically grown in clayey soils that retain water. The major rice-producing countries include China, India, and Indonesia.

☛ Air tissue found in rice roots → Aerenchyma
☛ Optimum temperature for rice cultivation → 20-37°C
☛ Scientific name of rice → Oryza sativa
☛ Largest producer of rice in the world → China
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी फसल जलभराव की स्थिति में उगाई जाती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: The Northern Plains of India are primarily formed by the deposits of which rivers? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Narmada and Tapti
Ganga, Indus and Brahmaputra
Yamuna and Chambal
Krishna and Godavari
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ganga, Indus and Brahmaputra

Explanation:
The Northern Plains of India were formed by the alluvial deposits brought down by three major river systems — the Ganga, the Indus, and the Brahmaputra — along with their tributaries. This vast plain covers about 7 lakh square kilometers. The Ganga basin is known for fertile alluvial soil, the Indus valley is famous for irrigation, and the Brahmaputra enters the eastern part to form the Assam valley. These rivers originate from the Himalayas and deposit silt, making the region highly fertile for agriculture. The plains are divided into Bhabar, Terai, Bangar, and Khadar zones based on the age and nature of deposits.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Area of Northern Plains? → About 7 lakh sq km
☛ Origin of Ganga river? → Gangotri Glacier (Uttarakhand)
☛ Countries flowed by Indus river? → Tibet, India, Pakistan
☛ Entry point of Brahmaputra in India? → Arunachal Pradesh (as Siang)
question_hi: भारत के उत्तरी मैदान मुख्य रूप से किन नदियों के निक्षेपों से बने हैं? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: What is the main cause of different seasons on the Earth?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Earth's distance from the Sun
Earth's rotation
Solar flares
Earth's tilt and revolution around the Sun
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Earth's tilt and revolution around the Sun

Explanation:
The Earth is tilted on its axis by 23.5° and revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. This tilt, combined with the revolution, causes different seasons. When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, it experiences summer, and when the Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, it experiences summer. The distance from the Sun has a negligible effect because Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in January, yet the Northern Hemisphere experiences winter. Earth's rotation only causes day and night, and solar flares are unrelated to seasons.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Earth's axial tilt → 23.5°
☛ Summer solstice → June 21 (longest day in Northern Hemisphere)
☛ Winter solstice → December 22 (shortest day in Northern Hemisphere)
☛ Perihelion → Earth closest to Sun (January 3-4)
☛ Aphelion → Earth farthest from Sun (July 4-5)

Explanation:
पृथ्वी अपनी धुरी पर 23.5° झुकी हुई है और सूर्य के चारों ओर दीर्घवृत्तीय कक्षा में घूमती है। यह झुकाव और परिक्रमा मिलकर विभिन्न ऋतुओं का कारण बनते हैं। जब उत्तरी गोलार्ध सूर्य की ओर झुका होता है, तो वहाँ ग्रीष्म ऋतु होती है, और जब दक्षिणी गोलार्ध झुका होता है, तो वहाँ ग्रीष्म ऋतु होती है। सूर्य से दूरी का प्रभाव नगण्य है, क्योंकि पृथ्वी जनवरी में सूर्य के सबसे निकट (पेरिहेलियन) होती है, फिर भी उत्तरी गोलार्ध में सर्दी होती है। पृथ्वी का घूर्णन केवल दिन-रात का कारण बनता है, और सौर ज्वालाएँ ऋतुओं से असंबंधित हैं।

question: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Green Revolution in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Increased use of fertilisers and irrigation
Expansion of agricultural land
Mechanisation of agriculture
Use of high-yielding variety seeds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Expansion of agricultural land

Explanation:
The Green Revolution (1960s-1970s) aimed to increase agricultural productivity on existing land, not by expanding farmland. Its core features included the use of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds (e.g., wheat and rice), increased use of chemical fertilizers (e.g., urea), pesticides, and irrigation facilities (canals, tubewells). Additionally, mechanisation of agriculture (tractors, harvesters) was promoted. Led by Norman Borlaug, HYV seeds doubled per-hectare yields. The revolution was most successful in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. It focused on agricultural intensification rather than extensification (land expansion). Thus, expansion of agricultural land was not a feature, as the strategy was to boost output per unit area using modern inputs.

☛ Which crops were mainly targeted by the Green Revolution in India? → Wheat and Rice
☛ What type of seeds were used in the Green Revolution? → High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds

question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which two northeastern states of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Nagaland and Mizoram
Tripura and Nagaland
Tripura and Manipur
Tripura and Mizoram
solution:

Explanation:
The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° North latitude) passes through India and cuts across eight states. In the northeastern region, it passes through only two states: Tripura and Mizoram. In Tripura, it passes through the southern part, while in Mizoram, it runs through the middle of the state. The Tropic of Cancer divides India into two zones: the northern part lies in the temperate zone and the southern part in the tropical zone. This line passes through central India including Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. Other northeastern states like Nagaland, Manipur, and Assam lie to the north of this line.

question: Which of the following is located in the northern part of the Eastern Ghats?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Mahendragiri hills
Nilgiri hills
Doddabetta hills
Anaimalai hills
solution:

Explanation:
The Eastern Ghats are a mountain range running parallel to India's eastern coast, passing through Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. In the northern part of the Eastern Ghats, the Mahendragiri hills are located in Odisha, with an elevation of about 1,501 meters. The Nilgiri hills, Doddabetta, and Anaimalai hills are part of the Western Ghats. The Nilgiris lie at the junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka; Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiris; and Anaimalai is in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Thus, only Mahendragiri hills are in the northern part of the Eastern Ghats.

question: Sand dunes that form long ridges parallel to the coastline are most common ______________.  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: along low sedimentary coasts
in estuarine regions only
along high rocky coasts
along tectonic plate boundaries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is along low sedimentary coasts

Explanation:
Sand dunes that form long ridges parallel to the coastline are called longitudinal dunes or coastal dunes. They are most common along low sedimentary coasts where abundant sand is available and winds blow parallel to the shore. High rocky coasts lack sufficient sand, estuarine regions have limited dune formation, and tectonic plate boundaries are not conducive to dune development. These dunes are important coastal landforms and help protect the shoreline from erosion by acting as natural barriers. Their formation depends on the interaction of wind, sand supply, and coastal topography.

question: Wet farming is least likely to be found among which the following Indian states?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Haryana
Assam
Manipur
Tripura
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Haryana

Explanation:
Wet farming refers to agricultural practices that require abundant water supply, either from rainfall or irrigation, typically for crops like rice. It is common in regions with high rainfall or ample irrigation facilities. Haryana is a semi-arid state with low annual rainfall (around 500-600 mm), making it the least likely for wet farming. In contrast, Assam, Manipur, and Tripura are northeastern states with heavy rainfall (over 2000 mm annually), supporting extensive rice cultivation and other wet crops. Haryana relies more on dry farming methods for crops like wheat and pulses. Wet farming is predominantly associated with rice paddies, which require standing water, a condition not typical in Haryana's climate.

question: Which of the following options explains the variation in temperature between coastal and interior parts of India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Altitude
Continentality
Pressure belts
Latitude
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Continentality

Explanation:
The variation in temperature between coastal and interior parts of India is primarily explained by continentality. Continentality refers to the difference in heating and cooling rates between land and water. Coastal regions, being near the sea, experience a maritime climate with less temperature fluctuation. In contrast, interior regions have a continental climate, characterized by very hot summers and very cold winters. While altitude, pressure belts, and latitude also affect temperature, the main factor for coastal-interior temperature difference is continentality.

question: Which of the following mass movements occurs when saturated soil and debris flow down a slope during heavy rainfall? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Avalanche
Mudflow
Soil creep
Rockfall
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mudflow

Explanation:
When saturated soil and debris flow rapidly down a slope during heavy rainfall, this mass movement is called mudflow. It is a type of mass wasting where water-saturated soil, rock fragments, and debris combine into a fluid, muddy flow. Mudflows are common in hilly and mountainous regions after heavy rains or rapid snowmelt. Avalanches involve snow and ice; soil creep is an extremely slow, gradual movement; and rockfall is the rapid falling of rocks. Mudflow moves at a fast pace and can carry large amounts of material, making it a destructive geological process.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What causes a mudflow? → Heavy rainfall leading to water-saturated soil
☛ What is soil creep? → Very slow, imperceptible downslope movement of soil
☛ What does an avalanche involve? → Snow and iceWhat is rockfall? → Rapid falling of rocks from a cliff
☛ What is mass wasting? → Downslope movement of rock, soil, or debris under gravity

question: What type of rocks mainly compose the Peninsular Plateau of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Recent volcanic lava deposits from plate margins
Layers of limestone and sandstone from marine origin
Old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks
Young sedimentary rocks formed in coastal plains
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks

Explanation:
The Peninsular Plateau of India is composed of ancient rocks from the Precambrian era. It mainly consists of crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks, which are highly hard and resistant. As a part of Gondwanaland, this landmass is very old and includes granite, gneiss, schist, basalt, etc. These rocks are rich in mineral resources. The plateau is one of the most stable landforms in India.

question: Ramsar convention is related to which of the following? (RRB JE ME (31/08/2019) CBT 2)
options: Forests
Wetlands
Animal Protection
Ozone Depletion
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wetlands

Explanation:
The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. It is named after Ramsar, Iran, where it was signed. This convention is not related to forests, animal protection, or ozone depletion.

question: Most of the _______ are formed by sand and silt deposited by rivers and sea waves. (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Laterite and lateritic soils
Alluvial soils
Peaty and Marshy soils
Saline and alkaline soils
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial soils

Explanation:
Alluvial soils are formed by sand and silt deposited by rivers and sea waves. They are the most fertile soils in India and are found in the northern plains, river valleys, and coastal areas. These soils are rich in potash and lime but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus. They are formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers, known as alluvium. Alluvial soils are classified into two types: Khadar (new alluvium) and Bhangar (old alluvium). Major crops grown include wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

☛ Where are alluvial soils most commonly found? → In the northern plains and river valleys of India
☛ Which major crops are grown in alluvial soils? → Wheat, rice, sugarcane, pulses

question: What is the fragrance of soil generated immediately after the rains?A. PetrichorB. Tempus vemumC. VrochiD. Irida (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: D
B
A
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Petrichor

Explanation:
The earthy scent produced when rain falls on dry soil is called Petrichor. The term is derived from Greek words 'petra' (stone) and 'ichor' (the fluid that flows in the veins of gods). This smell is primarily caused by a compound called geosmin, which is produced by soil-dwelling bacteria of the genus Streptomyces. When raindrops hit dry soil, they trap tiny air bubbles that carry geosmin upward, releasing the scent into the air. Humans are highly sensitive to this smell. The concept was first described by Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and Roderick Thomas in 1964.

☛ Who coined the term Petrichor? → Isabel Joy Bear and Roderick Thomas

question: 49th parallel line is a boundary between: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: India and Pakistan
North Korea and South Korea
USA and Canada
France and Germany
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is USA and Canada

Explanation:
The 49th parallel north is a circle of latitude that forms the border between USA and Canada. This boundary was established by the Convention of 1818 and the Oregon Treaty of 1846. It extends from Minnesota to the Pacific Ocean. The line separates the United States to the south and Canada to the north. It is one of the longest undefended borders in the world. Other options are incorrect: the India-Pakistan border is the 'Radcliffe Line', the North-South Korea border is the '38th parallel', and the France-Germany border is marked by natural features.

question_hi: 49वीं समानांतर रेखा _________के बीच की सीमा है। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options_hi: भारत और पाकिस्तान
उत्तर कोरिया और दक्षिण कोरिया
संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका और कनाडा
फ्रांस और जर्मनी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका और कनाडा

Explanation:
49वीं समानांतर रेखा यूएसए और कनाडा के बीच की सीमा है। यह रेखा अक्षांश के 49 डिग्री उत्तर पर स्थित है और 1818 के सम्मेलन तथा 1846 की ओरेगन संधि द्वारा निर्धारित की गई थी। यह सीमा मिनेसोटा से प्रशांत महासागर तक फैली हुई है। इस रेखा के दक्षिण में संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका और उत्तर में कनाडा स्थित है। यह दुनिया की सबसे लंबी असुरक्षित सीमाओं में से एक है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमा 'रेडक्लिफ रेखा' है, उत्तर-दक्षिण कोरिया सीमा '38वीं समानांतर' है, और फ्रांस-जर्मनी सीमा प्राकृतिक सीमाओं द्वारा चिह्नित है।
